name: El Palace Hotel
positioning: El Palace Barcelona, the hotel once known as the Ritz of Barcelona, steps from Passeig de Gràcia, with suites tied to artists who stayed there
best_for: Travelers interested in art and hotel history
Families who want a multi-bedroom suite

facts.text: Joan Miró was a regular at the hotel in the 1970s, when it was known as the Ritz of Barcelona.
Politician Francesc Cambó insisted that Barcelona needed a first-class hotel like the Ritz in Madrid, with the 1929 Barcelona International Exposition pending.
The hotel is just steps from Passeig de Gràcia.
The restaurant Amar Barcelona is by chef Rafa Zafra.
The hotel serves Afternoon Tea in the British style.
El Jardín is the hotel's breakfast garden.
Art Suites and El Palace Suites include a private check-in airport transfer, butler service and a champagne welcome.
Art Suites and El Palace Suites are offered with one or two bedrooms, each with a separate living and dining area.
Classic Rooms have an original 1919 fireplace chosen by César Ritz for the hotel's first design.
Classic Rooms have full soundproofing and open onto a French balcony with city views.
The Three-Bedroom Family Suite joins two Junior Suites and one Single Room by a private corridor.
The Joan Miró Art Suite is known as the Golden Suite.

highlights.text: Salvador Dalí once sent a taxidermied white horse up the hotel's main staircase as a birthday present for his wife, Gala.
Dalí was a frequent guest in the 1970s and photographed models in the same Roman bath that is in his suite today; the suite preserves the original decor from his stays.
The Ronnie Wood suite is an Art Deco suite that was once home to the Rolling Stones guitarist.
The Art Suites have an original Roman-style bathroom from 1919, restored in each suite.
The Rooftop Garden has panoramic views, and the hotel has a Mayan-inspired spa.

considerations.text: Superior Suite windows overlook the inner courtyard of the Eixample, while Classic Rooms open onto a French balcony with city views.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes a historic building with traditional room layouts.
